zh: 贵湖大学，位于加拿大安大略省贵湖市，是加拿大一所规模中等却有著全面教育的公立大学. 贵湖大学建立于1964年，由安大略省政府通过法案将安大略农业学院（OAC）和安大略兽医学院（OVC）及麦当劳学院（Macdonald Institute）合并而成贵湖大学. 当中的安大略兽医学院（OVC）更是目前加拿大全国五所兽医学院之一，安省唯一的兽医学院. 贵湖大学提供超过90个主修科（majors），13个荣誉学位及63个海外遥距课程.

根据Maclean's杂志，贵湖大学排名为加拿大第四的全面性大学. 更在1999，2002，2003，2006，2007年度在此排名中名列第一. 学校享有“全加本科教育质量第一”的名誉，更以“宽进严出”、高淘汰率的研究生高等教育（包括硕士和博士）而出名. 英语暨戏剧研究学校（School of English and Theatre Studies）在加拿大的文学及剧作和理论等学术领域方面位于领先，相当多的杰出人才任教于此.

安大略政府于1874年向Frederick William Stone购入五百英亩的土地以建立农业学校，安大略农业学校（Ontario School of Agriculture）于1874年五月一日在此预定地正式启用. * 1880年，名称改为安大略农业学院暨实验农场（Ontario Agricultural College and Experimental Farm）. * 1903年，麦当劳学院（Macdonald Institute）加入 * 1922，安大略兽医学院（Ontario Veterinary College）加入，OVC为北美最早成立的兽医学院，本于1862年在多伦多成立 * 1964年五月八日，贵湖大学法案于安大略立法部通过，将三个学院整合为一个大学，由董事会（Board of Governors）及理事会（The Senate）两个组织共同管理，前者负责行政及资金事务，后者负责学习事务 * 1964年理事会创立威灵顿学院（Wellington College），提供艺术及科学课程，五年后此学员的三个科系分开为艺术学院（College of Arts），物理科学学院（College of Physical Science）及社会科学学院（College of Social Science）. 麦当劳学院（Macdonald Institute）也在此时变更为家庭及消费者研究学院（College of Family and Consumer Studies） * 1971年，生物科学学院（College of Biological Science）由体适能教育学校（School of Physical Education），安大略农业学院的营养学系（OAC's Department of Nutrition）以及部分的植物学系微生物学系动物学系（Departments of Botany, Microbiology and Zoology）所组成 * 1989年，安大略农业学院的工程学校（OAC's school of Engineering）与物理科学学院（College of Physical Sciences）合并为物理暨工程科学学院（College of Physical & Engineering Sciences） * 1998年，家庭及消费者研究学院（College of Family and Consumer Studies）与社会科学学院（College of Social Science）合并为社会暨应用人类科学学院（College of Social & Applied Human Sciences） * 2006，商业，经济及管理课程（programs in business, economics and management）被独立整合出来成为管理暨经济学院（College of Management & Economics）

贵湖大学目前由七个学院组成，包含： * 文学院（College of Arts） * 生物科学学院（College of Biological Science） * 管理暨经济学院（College of Management & Ecomomics） * 物理暨工程科学学院（College of Physical & Engineering Science） * 社会暨应用人类科学学院（College of Social & Applied Human Sciences） * 安大略农业学院（Ontario Agricultural College） * 安大略兽医学院（Ontario Veterinary College）
en: The University of Guelph (U of G) is a comprehensive public research university in Guelph, in Ontario, Canada. It was established in 1964 after the amalgamation of Ontario Agricultural College (1874), the MacDonald Institute (1903), and the Ontario Veterinary College (1922), and has since grown to an institution of over 30,000 students from more than 140 countries (including those at the Humber campus, Ridgetown campus, off-campus degree enrolments, diploma enrolments and part-time students) and employs 823 full-time faculty (academic staff) as of 2025. It offers 94 undergraduate degrees, 48 graduate programs, and 6 associate degrees in many different disciplines.

The university conducts a significant degree of research and offers a wide range of undergraduate, graduate, and professional degrees. According to the Journal of Hospitality & Tourism Research, the university's Hospitality and Tourism Management program has Canada's highest research index.

The faculty at the University of Guelph hold 23 Canada Research Chair positions in the research areas of natural sciences, engineering, health sciences and social sciences. Academic achievements include the first scientific validation of water on Mars, Alpha Particle X-ray Spectrometer (APXS) on board the Curiosity rover, and the Barcode of Life project for species identification.

The University of Guelph traces its origins back to when the Ontario government bought 500 acre of farmland from Frederick William Stone and opened the Ontario School of Agriculture on May 1, 1874, which was renamed the Ontario Agricultural College (OAC) in 1880. The Experimental Farm has been part of the original project along with the museum of agriculture and horticulture. Its first building was Moreton Lodge, located where Johnston Hall now stands, which included classrooms, residences, a library, and a dining room. In 1874, the school started an apiculture department, teaching students about bees and beekeeping, in a dedicated building. In more recent years, the program has continued at the Honey Bee Research Centre located in the Arboretum, continuing research on honeybee health, providing apiculture and beekeeping courses and offering "many other educational experiences" including informative videos for beekeepers.

The Macdonald Institute was established in 1903 to house women's home economics programs, nature studies, and some domestic art and science. It was named after its financier, Sir William Macdonald, who worked to promote domestic sciences in rural Canada, and founded Macdonald College and McGill University College of British Columbia. The Ontario Veterinary College (OVC), founded in Mimico in 1862, was moved to Guelph in 1922. Economist John Kenneth Galbraith was an undergraduate at the college (graduating in 1931). In 1919 the Ontario Agricultural College aimed at recruiting "farm boys" with a low cost, two-year program ($20.00 per year) and "the lowest possible rate" for room and board.
